label: European LGM lakes and rivers (published vectors, experimental)
datum: lake levels in metres above mean sea level as in ETOPO1 (estimated from each lake's shore); outlines in WGS84 degrees
summary: European LGM lakes and rivers: one published snapshot (CRC806, compiled maps), 26.5–19 ka BP only; lakes keep groups out, fresh ones and the rivers count as fresh water. No Black Sea in the data.

epochs.name: LGM snapshot
epochs.state: one snapshot of the published LGM reconstruction, held unchanged through the window; never interpolated
epochs.water: lakes: fresh (assumed) except the Caspian, Aral, Sarygamysh and Lisan; rivers: fresh (assumed)

level.rule: per lake: median ETOPO1 height of its shore pixels, whole metres, carried as green * 256 + blue - 32768

mask.grid: 8640 x 4320 world pixels of 2.5'; x0, y0 = column, row of the patch's north-west pixel (row 0 north, column 0 180 W)

distance.grid: 4320 x 2160 HYDE 5' cells; x0, y0 = column, row of the patch's north-west cell
distance.encoding: water_distance.json: metres = max_metres * (code / 255) ** 2, code 0 = water in the cell
distance.rule: min(static distance image, distance to LGM rivers and fresh lakes); outside the patch the static image is exact

outside_epochs: scenario inactive: the geography is unknown at that date, which is not the same as dry; the app draws and places as it does without the flag
licence: CC-BY (CRC806 metadata PDF; dataset page: attribution required, commercial use and derivations allowed); version not stated

sources.data: Verheul, J., Zickel, M., Becker, D., Willmes, C. (2015): LGM major inland waters of Europe - GIS dataset. CRC806-Database, doi:10.5880/SFB806.14
sources.levels: ETOPO1 4' (data/raw/etopo/etopo_4min.nc), median of each lake's shore pixels
sources.chronology: the dataset's temporal metadata: LGM, 26,500-19,000 yBP (Clark et al. 2009); taken as calendar BP from 1950

uncertainty: One reconstruction stands for 7,500 years: lakes filled, drained and moved with the ice front inside the window.
Outlines come from maps of different scales and authors; some river reaches are GEBCO flow routes, not observed channels.

Lake levels are the median modern height of each outline's shore, not dated shorelines (they only set the close-up's water plane): the Polish ice-dammed lakes come out 30-60 m below the altitudes their sources state, Lake Lisan at -263 m where its LGM stand was nearer -160 m; the Caspian and Aral outlines are much larger than today and their LGM-age stands are debated.
Freshness is assumed from the lake's kind (ice-dammed and river lakes fresh; the Caspian, Aral, Sarygamysh and Lisan not).
The Black Sea is not in the dataset: its LGM level is not modelled here.
Nothing is said outside the window: not dry, not wet.

terrain.path: /terrain/pastwater/earth_{year}.webp (terrain_image.py --pastwater); other years use the ordinary images
